message.content:
The human skull consists of **22 bones** (or 29 if including the inner ear bones and hyoid bone). These bones are divided into two main groups: the **cranium (neurocranium)** and the **facial skeleton (viscerocranium)**.

## Cranium (Neurocranium) — 8 Bones

The cranium forms the protective housing for the brain, meninges, and cerebral vasculature. It consists of:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal bone** (1) | Forms the forehead and anterior portion of the skull roof; contains frontal sinuses |
| **Parietal bones** (2) | Form the sides and roof of the cranial vault |
| **Temporal bones** (2) | Form the sides and base of the cranium; contain structures of the middle and inner ear |
| **Occipital bone** (1) | Forms the back and base of the skull; contains the foramen magnum |
| **Sphenoid bone** (1) | Butterfly-shaped bone at the base of the skull; contains the sella turcica (houses pituitary gland) |
| **Ethmoid bone** (1) | Located between the orbits; forms part of the nasal cavity and contains the cribriform plate |

The cranium can be further subdivided into:
- **Calvaria (skullcap)** — the roof, formed by frontal, parietal, and occipital bones
- **Cranial base** — the floor, formed by frontal, sphenoid, ethmoid, occipital, parietal, and temporal bones

## Facial Skeleton (Viscerocranium) — 14 Bones

The facial skeleton forms the structure of the face and supports the openings of the respiratory and digestive tracts:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Maxillae** (2) | Form the upper jaw, part of the orbit, and most of the hard palate |
| **Zygomatic bones** (2) | Form the cheekbones and part of the lateral walls of the orbits |
| **Nasal bones** (2) | Form the bridge of the nose |
| **Lacrimal bones** (2) | Small bones in the medial walls of the orbits; house the lacrimal sac |
| **Palatine bones** (2) | Form the posterior part of the hard palate |
| **Inferior nasal conchae** (2) | Project into the nasal cavity; aid in airflow regulation |
| **Vomer** (1) | Forms the inferior portion of the nasal septum |
| **Mandible** (1) | The lower jaw; the **only movable bone** of the skull |

## Additional Associated Bones

- **Hyoid bone** — Located in the neck; not part of the skull proper, but often associated with it. Provides attachment for muscles of the tongue and larynx
- **Auditory ossicles** (6 total: 3 in each ear) — Malleus, incus, and stapes in the middle ear

## Key Sutures (Joints Between Bones)

- **Coronal suture** — between frontal and parietal bones
- **Sagittal suture** — between the two parietal bones
- **Lambdoid suture** — between parietal and occipital bones
- **Squamous suture** — between parietal and temporal bones

## Important Openings (Foramina)

| Opening | Structure(s) Passing Through |
|---------|------------------------------|
| Foramen magnum | Spinal cord, vertebral arteries |
| Optic canal | Optic nerve, ophthalmic artery |
| Foramen rotundum | Maxillary nerve |
| Foramen ovale | Mandibular nerve |
| Jugular foramen | Internal jugular vein, cranial nerves IX, X, XI |
| Carotid canal | Internal carotid artery |

Sources:
1. https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/the-skull
2. https://www.osmosis.org/learn/Bones_of_the_cranium
3. https://teachmeanatomy.info/head/osteology/skull/
4. https://www.numberanalytics.com/blog/skull-bones-anatomy-histology-explored
5. https://www.acibademhealthpoint.com/the-back-of-head-bones-understanding-cranial-anatomy/
6. https://anatomynote.com/the-human-skull-an-anatomical-masterpiece/
7. https://anatomy.co.uk/skull
